```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The bar is one paying customer in 90 days, and only Brief B shows that its payer type actually pays. Individuals pay Roam $15/mo or $180/yr (sourced via Vendr), and Obsidian sells paid Sync, Publish and Commercial tiers. Brief A states outright that 'no one is currently shown paying for Free Pascal/Lazarus documentation.'",
    "Brief A's only named institutional payer, the Free Pascal and Lazarus Foundation, is described in its own brief as funding development, not docs. That leaves only an unevidenced hypothetical: commercial Lazarus shops buying a hosted docs product.",
    "Brief A has its own unresolved structural blocker. A 2012 thread suggests maintainer unwillingness, not tooling, is the real bottleneck, and an outside site cannot fix that. It also flags that the addressable population may be too small to sustain revenue.",
    "Brief B names concrete, priced acquisition channels aimed at a large audience. Product Hunt costs $200–$2,000 and productivity YouTube sponsorships run $20–$40 CPM, both sourced. Brief A relies on unpaid forum posting at 'high time cost' and a generic, non-Pascal $2.69 CPC benchmark from 2016.",
    "Brief B's risks are serious: saturation, a free Obsidian status quo, WorldBrain's lack of mainstream traction, and Tana's pivot. But they bear on reaching scale, not on landing a first paying user. A narrow, opinionated niche product at $10–15/mo can plausibly convert a handful of enthusiasts within 90 days."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Brief A's payer and price evidence. The ~$50/month business tier is anchored to Read the Docs Business pricing, a different product serving a different audience. No source shows any Lazarus-based company, or anyone at all, willing to pay for Pascal documentation. Its demand quotes show pain, not willingness to pay, and at least one is from 2010.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate confidence. Brief B also has thin demand evidence: two anecdotes, neither showing willingness to pay for a new entrant. The Obsidian ~1M user figure is an estimate cited to Wikipedia. The claim that WorldBrain attracted funding is cited only to a GitHub repo, which may not support it. B wins mainly because its category has documented paying individuals, while A has none."
}
```
